title: Why Do You Waver?
subtitle: Raag Tilang
summary: This shabad meets fear with tenderness, not scolding. The repeated logic is simple: the One who made you has not stopped caring for you.
whyItMatters: It is a high-trust shabad for fear, panic, loneliness, and inner instability.
takeaway: The answer to fear is not bravado. It is remembrance of the One already holding you.

lines.translation: Merciful, the Lord Master is Merciful.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੀਅ ਸਗਲ ਕਉ ਦੇਇ ਦਾਨੁ ॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: jeea sagal kau dhei dhaan || rahaau ||
lines.translation: He gives His gifts to all beings. ||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੂ ਕਾਹੇ ਡੋਲਹਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀਆ ਤੁਧੁ ਰਾਖੈਗਾ ਸਿਰਜਣਹਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: too kaahe ddoleh praaneeaa tudh raakhaigaa sirajanahaar ||
lines.translation: Why do you waver, O mortal being? The Creator Lord Himself shall protect you.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਨਿ ਪੈਦਾਇਸਿ ਤੂ ਕੀਆ ਸੋਈ ਦੇਇ ਆਧਾਰੁ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: jin paidhais too keeaa soiee dhei aadhaar ||1||
lines.translation: He who created you, will also give you nourishment. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਨਿ ਉਪਾਈ ਮੇਦਨੀ ਸੋਈ ਕਰਦਾ ਸਾਰ ॥
lines.transliteration: jin upaiee medhanee soiee karadhaa saar ||
lines.translation: The One who created the world, takes care of it.

lines.gurmukhi: ਘਟਿ ਘਟਿ ਮਾਲਕੁ ਦਿਲਾ ਕਾ ਸਚਾ ਪਰਵਦਗਾਰੁ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: ghaT ghaT maalak dhilaa kaa sachaa paravadhagaar ||2||
lines.translation: In each and every heart and mind, the Lord is the True Cherisher. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਨਿ ਕੀਤਾ ਤਿਸਹਿ ਨ ਜਾਨਈ ਮਨਮੁਖਿ ਪਚਿ ਮੁਏ ਗਵਾਰ ॥
lines.transliteration: jin keetaa tiseh na jaanee manamukh pach mue gavaar ||
lines.translation: The self-willed fools do not know the One who created them; they rot away and die.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਵਣ ਜਾਣਾ ਨਾ ਥੀਐ ਪੂਰੇ ਗੁਰ ਦਰਬਾਰ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: aavan jaanaa na theeaai poore gur dharabaar ||3||
lines.translation: The cycle of coming and going in reincarnation is ended, in the Court of the Perfect Guru. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੂ ਕਾਹੇ ਡੋਲਹਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀਆ ਵੇਪਰਵਾਹੁ ਰਖੈਗਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: too kaahe ddoleh praaneeaa veparavaahu rakhaigaa ||
lines.translation: Why do you waver, O mortal being? The Lord who needs no care will care for you.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਦਾਸੁ ਚਰਨੀ ਲਾਗਾ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਪਰਬਤੁ ਠਹਰੈਗਾ ॥੪॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: naanak dhaas charanee laagaa saahib parabat Thaharaiagaa ||4||1||
lines.translation: Servant Nanak falls at His Feet; the Lord and Master stands firm like a mountain. ||4||1||

structure: Begins by naming the Lord as merciful before addressing fear directly.
Answers wavering by reminding the listener of the Creator's care.
Repeats the central reassurance in a steadier, more anchored form near the end.

evidence.coreClaim: This shabad meets fear with tenderness, not scolding. The repeated logic is simple: the One who made you has not stopped caring for you.
evidence.turn: Answers wavering by reminding the listener of the Creator's care.
evidence.practicalImplication: The answer to fear is not bravado. It is remembrance of the One already holding you.
